objectives: Explain what an IP address, a subnet and a port identify, using the CybICS lab network
Describe how a TCP connection starts and why a port scanner sends SYN packets
Explain why the attack machine on the flat CybICS lab network can reach every service
takeaways: The address finds the computer and the port the program: 172.18.0.3:502 is Modbus on the PLC.
Every packet carries both, nested in envelopes, and TCP shakes hands before any data flows.
On the flat lab network, any port the attack machine reaches is a port it can use.

checkpoints.question: Which of these addresses is NOT on the CybICS lab network 172.18.0.0/24?
checkpoints.explanation: With /24 the first three numbers must be 172.18.0. In 172.18.1.5 the third number is 1, so it is a different street. 172.18.0.50 looks unfamiliar because no CybICS service uses it, but it is on the right street; only the house number is new.

checkpoints.question: A scanner sends a SYN to a port of 172.18.0.3 and gets a reset (RST) back. What does that tell it?
options: The host answers, but the port is closed
The port is open and waits for data
There is no device at that address at all
checkpoints.explanation: An RST is the host saying "no one listens here": the computer is up, the port is closed. An open port would answer with SYN-ACK. A missing device cannot send anything, so it leads to silence, not to a reset.

quiz.question: OpenPLC is 172.18.0.3 and FUXA is 172.18.0.4. What do the shared first three numbers tell you?
options: Both sit on one and the same network
Both run on the same physical machine
Both listen on the same port number
Both share one network card and MAC
quiz.explanation: With a /24 subnet the first three numbers name the network, so both devices are on the same street and can talk directly. In the virtual lab they happen to run on one machine as well, but the address does not say so: in a real plant the same numbers usually belong to two separate boxes. Each container has its own network card and MAC address.

quiz.question: A packet reaches 172.18.0.3 with destination port 4840. What happens to it?
options: No program listens there, so it is refused
OpenPLC hands it on to the OPC-UA server
The PLC treats it as Modbus, its main protocol
It goes to whichever program is least busy
quiz.explanation: The port picks the program, and OpenPLC has nothing listening on 4840, so the connection is refused with a reset. The OPC-UA server listens on port 4840 of a different address, 172.18.0.5; a computer does not forward packets for a port it does not serve. Modbus only receives what is sent to port 502.

quiz.question: A scanner sends a SYN to 172.18.0.3 port 502 and receives a SYN-ACK. What has it learned?
options: A program is listening on port 502
The connection is fully set up now
The PLC accepted its Modbus login
Its Modbus request was delivered
quiz.explanation: A SYN-ACK is the second step of the handshake: something on that port is willing to talk, so the port is open. The connection is only complete after the scanner's ACK, which many scanners never send. No Modbus byte has travelled yet, and Modbus has no login to accept.

quiz.question: Which of these does a Modbus packet from the attack machine to the PLC carry?
options: The destination IP address 172.18.0.3
The destination port 502
A username and password for the PLC
The Modbus request itself
quiz.explanation: The IP envelope carries 172.18.0.3, the TCP envelope carries port 502, and the Modbus request sits in the middle. A login is the tempting extra, but none of the envelopes carries one: Modbus has none.

quiz.question: Why can the attack machine at 172.18.0.100 send Modbus requests straight to the PLC?
options: FUXA passes its requests on to the PLC
Both sit on one flat network, nothing in between
It first logs in to the PLC on port 502
The PLC trusts any address whose last number is 100
quiz.explanation: The attack machine shares the 172.18.0.0/24 network with the PLC, with no router or firewall between them, so it reaches port 502 directly. Logging in is the tempting idea, but Modbus has no login: reaching the port is enough. FUXA is just another client, and the PLC does not care about the last number.
